name: Clinical spin-warp magnetic resonance imaging
summary: Aberdeen's spin-warp method made magnetic resonance images of patients without X-rays, using an encoding scheme that became standard in clinical MRI.
description: Spin-warp magnetic resonance imaging uses fixed-duration phase encoding with varied gradient amplitude and Fourier reconstruction to form cross-sectional images without X-ray transmission.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

impact.note: A more robust encoding step within magnetic resonance imaging that became standard, so routine hospital scanning across many societies and later pulse sequences rest on it.

date.label: by 1980-08
date.basis: Latest supported availability or use; first possible entry is not established.

events.statement: Aberdeen researchers and clinicians used the spin-warp method to image a patient by August 1980.
events.caveats: A participant dates the first patient to 26 August 1980 and NHS Scotland dates a clinically useful image to 28 August; these may be distinct. Earlier human MR and multidimensional Fourier imaging predate spin-warp.

evidence.supports: A participant recalls an Aberdeen patient scan with 2D Fourier spin-warp on 26 August 1980.
NHS Scotland dates a clinically useful patient image to 28 August 1980.
The medical imaging method uses magnetic fields and radio waves rather than X-rays.
The author contrasts fixed-duration, variable-gradient spin-warp with earlier Fourier imaging.
Kumar, Welti and Ernst describe multidimensional Fourier NMR imaging in 1975.
